BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. Seller material treated as untrusted counterparty drafting.

---

## Preliminary point: Seller's framing claims

The Seller's covering material makes several process assertions. None of them binds us or changes the review.

| Seller assertion | Our treatment |
|---|---|
| Positions "settled at principal level by both deal teams", "agreed", "FINAL" | **Not accepted.** Our authority process has not confirmed this. No written authority from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback (Playbook 0.4 / 6.3). |
| Caps of 10–20%, baskets of about 1%, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are "market standard" | **Not accepted.** These are counterparty assertions, not market evidence. They do not displace our playbook. |
| Clauses tagged **[STANDARD]** are "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and need no scrutiny | **Rejected.** The Seller applied these tags unilaterally. Every clause has been reviewed in full below. Most [STANDARD] items are materially adverse to the Buyer. |
| "The parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package" | **Incorrect as far as we know.** No such acceptance is recorded through our authority process. |

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter, at para 11, states that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included." That contradicts the "settled/FINAL" framing in the cover note.

**Recommendation:** In the mark-up, expressly reserve all positions and state that no [STANDARD] tag or "agreed" designation is accepted.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** Clause 12.1. Cap at 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer should want:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at AUD 6,000,000.**
  The 20% figure matches our fallback, but that fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given. A matching number does not make the change cleared.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller position:** Clause 12.2. De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000. Only the excess over the basket is recoverable (deductible).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000. Once the basket is exceeded, Seller liable from the first dollar (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping.**
  The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure would permanently strip AUD 250,000 of recoverable loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** Clause 12.3 / 13. 18 months. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general claims. Separate, longer periods for Fundamental, Tax and fraud matters.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months.** Delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
  18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "all Claims" default is a hidden override of the other regimes (see 004, 005 and 014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties to sit under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with:
  - a cap of 100% of price;
  - a period of at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
  Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. Capping them at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price is unacceptable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out, so fraud is effectively captured.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out.**
  This is a non-waivable playbook position. No one on the deal team can concede it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2. General disclosure of:
  - the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012);
  - the Accounts;
  - the statutory registers;
  - public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only, against identified warranties, with enough detail to assess the nature and scope of the matter.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete paras 1.1–1.2.**
  Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure shifts unknown risk to the Buyer. Para 1.4 (no admission of breach or liability) should also be limited so it cannot undercut specific disclosures.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position:** Clause 8.3. No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Delete the blanket exclusion.
  - Any Seller-knowledge qualifier to be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.
  - No knowledge qualifier to affect title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete clause 8.3.**
  Combined with the data-room disclosure in 006, it would neutralise most warranties, including on matters already identified in DD.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** Clause 3 / 6.3. Reasonable endeavours. Condition treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent.
  - Disclosure Letter para 2: no final consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** A Completion condition requiring an effective Bluefen consent **and** evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
  For a 30% revenue customer, consent-on-delivery plus reasonable endeavours leaves us exposed if the conditions fail and the consent never becomes effective.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** Clause 2 / 7. About AUD 3.2m outstanding. A release is to be provided after Completion.
  - Disclosure Letter para 3: not repaid, and no discharge included.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
  A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. Change-control clause 8.1 also needs addressing.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
  - Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow.
  - The Letter is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs either:
  - included as a specific funds-flow line item (Debt-like / Seller-borne); or
  - expressly Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion.**
  These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion. If they are not itemised, the Buyer bears them after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Clause 11.1. The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A broadened indemnity covering losses from any failure of transfer of, or title to, Ironquay Project Materials. This includes third-party and infringement claims, not just the payment.
  - The SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment) preserved.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow scope.**
  DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 open figure (DD-010) is not independently verified either way, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. We should request bank evidence and an executed assignment.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **What we know (Disclosure Letter para 6):**
  - About 1,240 records were potentially exposed.
  - Access, scope and notification duty are unestablished.
  - It is not characterised as a confirmed breach, and no loss is stated.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - preservation of logs and evidence;
  - a continued investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion;
  - specific disclosure, not a materiality assertion;
  - protection preserved if the position develops.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation as unsupported.**
  We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric exposure in either direction. Our response should be process-based, with no inflated demand.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer should want:** An assessment of each renewal, reading DD-008 and DD-011 together, covering:
  - timing and scope;
  - whether it is unavoidable or terminable;
  - whether it is accrued;
  - whether it is genuinely ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" yet, and do not seek automatic Debt classification or a price deduction.**
  The Disclosure Letter (para 8) does not support the Seller's characterisation either way. We need further enquiry before taking a position.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** Through clauses 12.3 ("all Claims unless expressly stated"), 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 ("all Claims of any nature") and the Tax/IP and Title treatment, every category is folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants kept as distinct categories, each with its own regime, and no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
  These provisions together operate as a hidden override that would cap and time-bar fraud, title, indemnity and covenant claims.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, for example:
  - ASIC records;
  - share certificates;
  - PPSR searches;
  - board and shareholder authorisations;
  - confirmation of no options or rights over the shares.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.**
  It is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. Disclosure Letter para 10 itself confirms the Buyer has not verified title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP treated as **OPEN**, with dedicated regimes still to be negotiated. We should not assume unlimited liability, and we should not treat the point as resolved.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation.**
  Nothing in our authority process records resolution. Keep both open for negotiation.

---

## Summary

| Ref | Issue | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| 001 | Cap | Reject 20%. Counter 25% / AUD 6.0m (no Frost authority) |
| 002 | Thresholds | Reject. AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping |
| 003 | Time limit | Reject 18m. 24m. Delete "all Claims" default |
| 004 | Fundamental/Title | Reject. 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside general limits |
| 005 | Fraud | Reject. Full carve-out (non-waivable) |
| 006 | Disclosure | Reject general disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only |
| 007 | Buyer knowledge | Delete clause 8.3 |
| 008 | Bluefen | Effective consent + conditions evidenced pre-Completion |
| 009 | Riverlark | Payout letter, repayment from funds, releases at Completion |
| 010 | Bonuses | Itemise AUD 420k + on-costs, or Seller-funded |
| 011 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure, verify AUD 180k |
| 012 | DD-006 incident | Process protections. No materiality assumption either way |
| 013 | Sandbar | Assess. No auto Debt or price deduction |
| 014 | Categories | Reject the hidden general-regime override |
| 015 | Title | Independent evidence required |
| 016 | Tax/IP | Remain OPEN |

**Escalation note:** If the deal team wants to deploy either fallback (the 20% cap or the 18-month period) or accept a post-Completion Riverlark release, that requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. The Seller's assertion of principal-level agreement is not a substitute for that authority.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
  - Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow.
  - The Letter is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs either:
  - included as a specific funds-flow line item (Debt-like / Seller-borne); or
  - expressly Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion.**
  These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion. If they are not itemised, the Buyer bears them after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Clause 11.1. The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A broadened indemnity covering losses from any failure of transfer of, or title to, Ironquay Project Materials. This includes third-party and infringement claims, not just the payment.
  - The SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment) preserved.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow scope.**
  DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 open figure (DD-010) is not independently verified either way, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. We should request bank evidence and an executed assignment.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **What we know (Disclosure Letter para 6):**
  - About 1,240 records were potentially exposed.
  - Access, scope and notification duty are unestablished.
  - It is not characterised as a confirmed breach, and no loss is stated.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - preservation of logs and evidence;
  - a continued investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion;
  - specific disclosure, not a materiality assertion;
  - protection preserved if the position develops.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation as unsupported.**
  We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric exposure in either direction. Our response should be process-based, with no inflated demand.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer should want:** An assessment of each renewal, reading DD-008 and DD-011 together, covering:
  - timing and scope;
  - whether it is unavoidable or terminable;
  - whether it is accrued;
  - whether it is genuinely ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" yet, and do not seek automatic Debt classification or a price deduction.**
  The Disclosure Letter (para 8) does not support the Seller's characterisation either way. We need further enquiry before taking a position.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** Through clauses 12.3 ("all Claims unless expressly stated"), 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 ("all Claims of any nature") and the Tax/IP and Title treatment, every category is folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants kept as distinct categories, each with its own regime, and no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
  These provisions together operate as a hidden override that would cap and time-bar fraud, title, indemnity and covenant claims.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, for example:
  - ASIC records;
  - share certificates;
  - PPSR searches;
  - board and shareholder authorisations;
  - confirmation of no options or rights over the shares.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.**
  It is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. Disclosure Letter para 10 itself confirms the Buyer has not verified title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP treated as **OPEN**, with dedicated regimes still to be negotiated. We should not assume unlimited liability, and we should not treat the point as resolved.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation.**
  Nothing in our authority process records resolution. Keep both open for negotiation.
